doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Moving to New York with her husband and children; the West Coast sound
summary: She moved to New York with husband Charles and children, felt at home there, and recalls hearing Chico Hamilton, Mulligan, Baker and Getz in California.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So the pull of New York eventually got you I would imagine?
Yes. Well I was married then and my husband was from New York.
And he wanted to come back, yeah. So we came back and we already had three children so we brought them back and then I had a fourth one here.

No. No. It felt like that’s where I should have been from the beginning. Even though I love California, it’s beautiful, and being by the ocean, I have to be by the water. Even now you look out my apartment window and you see water. And I also have a beach house that reminds me of the place I was born. And it’s on the east coast but you know it’s kind of like I need both of those things: the busy, busy city and the very, very quiet by the ocean.
Do you think there is a west coast sound for jazz? You kind of always see that in the history books.

Well you know I mean the people that I heard probably because there was more west coast jazz. Friends introduced me to — I was talking to Chico Hamilton who teaches at the New School, telling him he was one of my first influences because it was Gerry Mulligan and Chet Baker and this is what I used to hear a lot of when I was say fifteen. I didn’t hear Bird until I was about seventeen, sixteen or seventeen. So yeah, I like that sound, and it did sound different. And Stan Getz was another one that I heard a lot of in California. So yeah, it did sound a lot different than the other thing, but I like them all. Every tune. I like a lot of different things.
